Depending on the floor design, controlling the initial temperature gradient in the floor could be a critical step for preserving structural integrity; therefore, flowing the fluid through an electrical heater could, in some cases, help improve the thermal profile of the initial fill process. In addition, the air preheating system may continue to operate, provided the pressure limitations of the tank are always respected; the air preheating system can significantly reduce heat losses during the initial salt fill, but as the salt approaches operational levels, the tank is generally not designed to have a pressurized headspace, and great care must be taken by the operator of the filling and air heating systems. For simulation purposes in the representative tank design, the reference temperature at the center of the tank floor is defined as the average temperature of the central portion of the floor to the outer radial position of the sparger ring.
